title: Life Care Center of Casper ranked No. 2 in Natrona County nursing homes in Q1 2026
text:
Life Care Center of Casper was identified as the second largest nursing home in Natrona County during the first quarter of 2026, tying with Casper Mountain Rehabilitation and Care Center, according to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) .
The facility had 120 beds available—24 fewer than Natrona County’s average in the same quarter. The center served an average of 76.3 residents over that period.
Life Care Center of Casper received an overall CMS rating of 5 out of 5, higher than the Wyoming nursing home state average of 3.
Shepherd of the Valley Rehabilitation and Wellness operated as the largest nursing home in Natrona County during the quarter, with 192 beds on site.
As of the first quarter of 2026, Life Care Center of Casper had no incidents resulting in fines or penalties.
There were 3 for-profit nursing homes in Natrona County, Wyoming, in total.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the country’s older adult population continues to expand as the population of younger age groups declines. Between 2020 and 2024, Americans age 65 and older increased by 13%, while those under 18 declined by 1.7%. The older segment of the population has seen significant growth in the past 100 years, rising from 4.9 million in 1920 to more than 61 million by 2024.
A 2021 analysis found that about half of older Americans, estimated at roughly 28 million, may need long-term services and supports. The same study predicts that over a third in this age group might eventually require nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
